title: Termwise change of rings preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes
statement: Let (C,J) be a site, O and O' sheaves of commutative rings, and phi: O → O' a ring morphism. Let E be an additive functor between their module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], whose objects and maps agree, with equality transports, with extension of scalars along phi [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For any quasi-isomorphism alpha: P → Q [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-flat cochain complexes of O-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], the termwise image E(alpha) is a quasi-isomorphism of O'-module complexes. No derived-category existence or counit is asserted.

source.place: Tag 06YT, proof, specialized to the target ring in degree zero; Tag 06YY, change-of-rings case

proof.text: The cone of alpha is acyclic by the cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. It is K-flat because cones of maps between K-flat complexes are K-flat [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum].
Apply extension-of-scalars acyclicity [lem-pur-change-of-rings-acyclic-kflat] to Cone(alpha). Its termwise E-image is acyclic.

An additive functor commutes with mapping cones: Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso alpha E identifies E(Cone(alpha)) with Cone(E(alpha)). Apply HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor in every degree to this isomorphism. IsZero.of_iso transports vanishing of homology to the latter cone. The cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] gives the desired QuasiIso. This is the actual Lean composition and uses no tensor-cone comparison in the parent module.
